clauseA.heading: Term and Duration
clauseA.rawText: The tenancy shall be for a fixed term of 11 (Eleven) continuous months commencing from 1st August 2026 and expiring on 30th June 2027. Any extension of the tenancy shall be solely subject to mutual written consent of both parties executed at least 30 days prior to the expiration of this Agreement.

clauseB.heading: Term and Duration
clauseB.rawText: The tenancy shall be for a fixed term of 11 (Eleven) continuous months commencing from 1st August 2026 and expiring on 30th June 2027. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written consent of both parties executed at least 30 days prior to expiration.

matchedPairs.difference: No substantive difference; both documents require mutual written consent 30 days prior to expiration to extend the tenancy.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: The language differences are stylistic and do not change the substantive rights or obligations of the parties.

verification.details: The comparison correctly identifies that the language differences are stylistic and not substantive.

clauseA.heading: Monthly Rent and Maintenance
clauseA.rawText: The Lessee agrees to pay a monthly rent of Rs. 38,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Eight Thousand only) exclusive of society maintenance charges. The rent shall be paid on or before the 5th day of every English calendar month into the Lessor's designated bank account. Any delay beyond the 5th day of the month shall attract a late penalty charge of Rs. 500/- per week of delay.

clauseB.heading: Monthly Rent and Maintenance
clauseB.rawText: The Lessee agrees to pay a monthly rent of Rs. 42,000/- (Rupees Forty-Two Thousand only) exclusive of society maintenance charges. The rent shall be paid on or before the 5th day of every English calendar month into the Lessor's designated bank account. Any delay beyond the 5th day of the month shall attract a late penalty charge of Rs. 1,000/- per week of delay.

matchedPairs.difference: Document A specifies a monthly rent of Rs. 38,000 and a late fee of Rs. 500 per week, whereas Document B specifies a higher monthly rent of Rs. 42,000 and a higher late fee of Rs. 1,000 per week.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: Document A is more favorable to the tenant as it provides for lower monthly rent and lower late penalty fees.

verification.details: The comparison accurately reports the numerical differences regarding rent and late fees found in both clauses.

clauseA.heading: Security Deposit
clauseA.rawText: The Lessee has paid an interest-free refundable security deposit of Rs. 1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand only) to the Lessor via RTGS transfer upon signing this Agreement. This deposit shall be refunded to the Lessee within 7 business days of peacefully vacating the Scheduled Premises, subject to deductions for unpaid rent, utility dues, and property damages.

clauseB.heading: Security Deposit
clauseB.rawText: The Lessee has paid an interest-free refundable security deposit of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) to the Lessor via RTGS transfer upon signing this Agreement. This deposit shall be refunded to the Lessee within 15 business days of peacefully vacating the Scheduled Premises, subject to deductions for unpaid rent and utility dues.

matchedPairs.difference: Document A requires a security deposit of Rs. 1,50,000 with a 7-day refund timeline, whereas Document B requires a higher deposit of Rs. 2,00,000 with a longer 15-day refund timeline and omits property damages as a specific ground for deduction.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: Document A is more favorable to the tenant due to the lower financial burden of the deposit and the significantly faster refund processing time.

verification.details: The comparison accurately highlights the differences in security deposit amount, refund timeline, and deduction criteria.

clauseA.heading: Lock-in Period and Notice for Termination
clauseA.rawText: Both parties agree to a mandatory Lock-in Period of 6 (six) months, during which neither party can terminate this Agreement. After completion of the lock-in period, either party may terminate the tenancy by serving 2 (two) months' prior written notice or by paying 2 months' rent in lieu thereof. If the Lessee vacates during the lock-in period, the Security Deposit shall stand forfeited up to the extent of the remaining lock-in rent.

clauseB.heading: Lock-in Period and Notice for Termination
clauseB.rawText: Both parties agree to a Lock-in Period of 3 (three) months, during which neither party can terminate this Agreement. After completion of the lock-in period, either party may terminate the tenancy by serving 1 (one) month's prior written notice or by paying 1 month's rent in lieu thereof.

matchedPairs.difference: Document A mandates a 6-month lock-in period with a 2-month notice/payment termination clause, while Document B mandates a shorter 3-month lock-in period with a 1-month notice/payment termination clause.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: Document B is more favorable to the tenant as it provides greater flexibility to terminate the lease earlier and requires less notice or financial penalty upon termination.

verification.details: The comparison accurately captures the differences in the lock-in periods and the notice requirements between the two clauses.

clauseA.heading: Utility and Consumption Charges
clauseA.rawText: The Lessee shall directly bear and promptly pay the monthly electricity consumption charges as billed by BESCOM, piped cooking gas charges, and internet subscription fees as per actual consumption throughout the tenure.

clauseB.heading: Utility and Consumption Charges
clauseB.rawText: The Lessee shall directly bear and promptly pay the monthly electricity consumption charges as billed by BESCOM, piped cooking gas charges, and internet subscription fees as per actual consumption throughout the tenure.

matchedPairs.difference: No substantive difference; both documents require the Lessee to bear electricity, gas, and internet costs as per actual consumption.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: The obligations regarding utility payments are identical in both documents.

verification.details: The comparison correctly identifies that the utility payment obligations are identical.

clauseA.heading: Repairs, Damages, and Indemnity
clauseA.rawText: The Lessee shall maintain the interior fixtures, sanitary fittings, and electrical appliances in tenantable condition. The Lessee shall be liable to compensate the Lessor for any structural damage, glass breakage, or fixture defacement caused by negligence. Minor routine repairs up to Rs. 1,000/- shall be borne by the Lessee, while major structural repairs shall be the Lessor's responsibility.

clauseB.heading: Repairs, Damages, and Indemnity
clauseB.rawText: The Lessee shall maintain the interior fixtures, sanitary fittings, and electrical appliances in tenantable condition. Minor routine repairs up to Rs. 1,000/- shall be borne by the Lessee, while major structural repairs shall be the Lessor's responsibility.

matchedPairs.difference: Document A explicitly holds the Lessee liable for structural damage, glass breakage, or fixture defacement caused by negligence, whereas Document B omits these specific liability examples.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: Document B is more favorable to the tenant as it removes specific categories of potential liability for damage.

verification.details: The comparison correctly identifies that Clause A includes specific damage liability clauses that are absent in Clause B.

clauseA.heading: Prohibited Activities and Subletting
clauseA.rawText: The Lessee covenants that the premises shall be used exclusively for residential purposes only. Subletting, re-letting, assigning, or parting with possession of the premises or any portion thereof to third parties or PG guests is strictly prohibited and shall constitute an incurable material breach.

clauseB.heading: Prohibited Activities and Subletting
clauseB.rawText: The Lessee covenants that the premises shall be used exclusively for residential purposes only. Subletting, re-letting, assigning, or parting with possession of the premises to third parties is strictly prohibited.

matchedPairs.difference: Document A explicitly prohibits subletting to PG guests and classifies such actions as an incurable material breach, whereas Document B provides a more general prohibition without mentioning PG guests or the specific breach classification.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: Document B is more favorable to the tenant because it is less restrictive and omits the harsh classification of a potential violation as an incurable material breach.

verification.details: The comparison accurately notes the differences regarding specific prohibitions and the classification of a breach.

clauseA.heading: Immediate Termination and Eviction
clauseA.rawText: If the Lessee fails to pay the monthly rent for 2 (two) consecutive months, or engages in illegal, unlawful, or nuisance activities affecting neighbors, the Lessor reserves the absolute right to terminate this agreement forthwith and re-enter and take possession of the premises without notice.

clauseB.heading: Immediate Termination and Eviction
clauseB.rawText: If the Lessee fails to pay the monthly rent for 2 (two) consecutive months, or engages in illegal activities, the Lessor reserves the right to terminate this agreement forthwith and re-enter and take possession of the premises.

matchedPairs.difference: Document A defines termination grounds to include nuisance activities and mentions the right to re-enter without notice, whereas Document B limits grounds to illegal activities and omits the 'without notice' phrasing.
matchedPairs.favorsReason: Document B is more favorable to the tenant by narrowing the scope of termination and removing the explicit 'without notice' re-entry clause.

verification.details: The comparison correctly identifies the differences in the scope of termination and the procedural requirement of notice.

clauseA.heading: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
clauseA.rawText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the Laws of India and the provisions of the Karnataka Rent Act. Any legal disputes arising under this agreement shall be subject exclusively to the civil courts of competent jurisdiction in Bengaluru.

clauseB.heading: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
clauseB.rawText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the Laws of India and the provisions of the Karnataka Rent Act. Any legal disputes shall be subject exclusively to the civil courts of competent jurisdiction in Bengaluru.

clause.heading: Painting and Maintenance Deductions
clause.rawText: At the time of vacating the premises, a mandatory non-negotiable deduction of Rs. 15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand only) or one month's rent (whichever is lower) shall be retained from the Security Deposit towards professional deep cleaning and repainting of the interior walls.

clause.heading: Pet Policy and Animal Regulations
clause.rawText: Keeping of any domestic animals or pets, including dogs, cats, or birds, within the Scheduled Premises is strictly prohibited under all circumstances without exception. Any unauthorized keeping of pets will lead to immediate lease cancellation and a penalty of Rs. 25,000/-.
